Bus Brothers

By: Anina Peens | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Rising poverty levels in small towns across the Northern Cape has been a hotbed for human traffickers prying on vulnerable girls

Summary:
More and more young women and teenagers are opting to work as prostitutes to be able to buy food. In some small and poverty stricken towns in the Northern and Western Cape, human traffickers are prying on this vulnerability. Girls are being targeted in towns along the N1 and N12 hiways between Johannesburg and Cape Town. They are being lured by traffickers who promise them lavish jobs and because of their desperation for work and income, it is not hard to convince them. They get into cars, taxis, buses and trucks voluntarily, and some are never seen again.

Further information:
The town of Touwsriver in the Western Cape is facing a massive socio-economic crisis. The most worrying of which is the rapid spike in prostitution amongst young residents, including teenagers. As a result of the extended drought, agriculture has collapsed in the area and left thousands of residents desperate. And human traffickers are having a field day. As the desperation grows, the number of people trafficked, rises. This is abundantly clear in Touwsriver as the town is situated on the N1 and provides stopovers for long distance travelers, including trucks.

The Hawks cracked down on a human trafficking house in Kuruman at the end of May and saved four girls who have been trafficked from various towns in the Northern Cape. According to the provincial unit of the Hawks, traffickers choose routes off the beaten tracks where roadblocks are unlikely. They also target the poorest of the poor communities. The unit says, prostitution has spiked in most small towns in the Northern Cape that are located near main hi-ways where long hauling trucks operate.

BUS BROTHERS DRAFT 3

VO

Between Johannesburg and Cape town, in the middle of the country, the N1 and its alternative, the N12, hold a bouquet of small towns between them. In the eye of a passer-through, these towns may be peaceful and quint, welcoming travelers to the iconic karoo. But where they stopover in the blissful silence, the voicelessness of desperation echoes.
This is central South Africa, and it seems that communities here have been completely forgotten, paving the way for shocking crimes that seem to go unnoticed.
Over the last seven months, Carte Blanche visited various towns in the central karoo, capturing a crime that is visible in plain sight, but at the same time, completely hidden.

This is central South Africa, and it seems that communities here have been completely forgotten, paving the way for shocking crimes that seem to go unnoticed. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Rising poverty levels in small towns across the Northern Cape has been a hotbed for human traffickers prying on vulnerable girls
metadata.Summary: More and more young women and teenagers are opting to work as prostitutes to be able to buy food. In some small and poverty stricken towns in the Northern and Western Cape, human traffickers are prying on this vulnerability. Girls are being targeted in towns along the N1 and N12 hiways between Johannesburg and Cape Town. They are being lured by traffickers who promise them lavish jobs and because of their desperation for work and income, it is not hard to convince them. They get into cars, taxis, buses and trucks voluntarily, and some are never seen again.
metadata.Further information: The town of Touwsriver in the Western Cape is facing a massive socio-economic crisis. The most worrying of which is the rapid spike in prostitution amongst young residents, including teenagers. As a result of the extended drought, agriculture has collapsed in the area and left thousands of residents desperate. And human traffickers are having a field day. As the desperation grows, the number of people trafficked, rises. This is abundantly clear in Touwsriver as the town is situated on the N1 and provides stopovers for long distance travelers, including trucks. The Hawks cracked down on a human trafficking house in Kuruman at the end of May and saved four girls who have been trafficked from various towns in the Northern Cape. According to the provincial unit of the Hawks, traffickers choose routes off the beaten tracks where roadblocks are unlikely. They also target the poorest of the poor communities. The unit says, prostitution has spiked in most small towns in the Northern Cape that are located near main hi-ways where long hauling trucks operate.
